quest.title: The Magic That Never Fails
quest.description: Thanks to everyone's efforts, you've made progress in the operation to save the imaginary friend...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Pals Synergy x60, Mora x50000, Hero's Wit x5

dialogues.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
dialogues.text: Alright, we're all set. The baku have been fasting all night, so we should be able to get rid of this nightmare no problem.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: These are the fragments we collected.

dialogues.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
dialogues.text: Mm, the scent matches what we found earlier. Yep, these are the ones. Here goes nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, looks like Popcorn is back to normal!

dialogues.speaker: Popcorn
dialogues.text: Phew... Finally, I don't feel so dizzy anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Popcorn
dialogues.text: I remember now... I remember everything! Thank you for keeping me company these past few days and helping Homura overcome her nightmare!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, our pleasure! How did you get separated from Homura, anyway? Aren't imaginary friends supposed to live inside kids' heads?

dialogues.speaker: Popcorn
dialogues.text: Well, actually... Homura is all grown up now...

dialogues.speaker: Popcorn
dialogues.text: Her work's been so busy and stressful — she can't even sleep most nights. And when she finally found some time to relax out in nature, she had a nightmare the minute she tried to take a nap...

dialogues.speaker: Popcorn
dialogues.text: I just wanted to give her a chance to rest, so I tried to get rid of the nightmare by going inside of it and beating up all the things tormenting her.

dialogues.speaker: Popcorn
dialogues.text: But then... I got swept up in a massive storm, and when Homura woke up, an ominous-looking shard was left behind, right where she was sleeping!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: The nightmare fragment.

dialogues.speaker: Popcorn
dialogues.text: Yeah! So, I tried to smash it to pieces!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess Popcorn's temper wasn't just the nightmare talking...

dialogues.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
dialogues.text: No, but it definitely made it more extreme.

dialogues.speaker: Popcorn
dialogues.text: But I failed again! Then, I got super dizzy, and well... You know the rest.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Well, we got rid of all the nightmare fragments, right? So is the problem solved?

dialogues.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
dialogues.text: Homura is free from the nightmare, but her psychological state is still abnormal... In fact, the problem could be quite serious.

dialogues.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
dialogues.text: While digesting the fragments just now, the baku sensed that there was no attempt from Homura to overcome the emotions contained within them... which is a sign of emotional numbness.

dialogues.speaker: Popcorn
dialogues.text: She hasn't given a sincere smile in ages. She doesn't let her imagination run wild like she did as a kid, or think up crazy scenes in her head...

dialogues.speaker: Popcorn
dialogues.text: I can't encourage her through her imagination like I used to... All I can do is watch her lose her spark.

dialogues.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
dialogues.text: When someone gives up on seeking and relishing in their own happiness, negative emotions can become all-consuming. And if that happens...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...What? If that happens, then what?

dialogues.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
dialogues.text: We see patients like this a lot at the clinic. On the outside, it might seem like nothing is wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
dialogues.text: But on the inside, a sense of emptiness begins to take over, until the person loses the capacity to recognize beauty in the world.

dialogues.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
dialogues.text: As one of our patients put it: "It's not that I'm gone, it's the knowledge that my inner child is never coming back."

dialogues.speaker: Popcorn
dialogues.text: No, no! I have to help her!

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Where did she go? Will she be back for dinner?

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: No, Qiqi. That was just a metaphor or, um... personification? One of the two.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Who says she can't come back! Sometimes after I get let out of confinement, I dash off so fast even Master Jean can't catch me!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: But then, Dodoco reminds me that's a sure-fire way to get sent back to confinement, so I turn around and go back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that's a more... literal take, but Paimon thinks the logic still applies!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Yeah, I think so too. If anyone has a chance of getting through to her, it'd be Popcorn, right? He is her imaginary friend, after all. She has to listen to him.

dialogues.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
dialogues.text: True. I'd hate for her to get to the point of needing professional help. If she can work through these problems on her own, even better.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Popcorn said Homura hasn't thought about him in ages... She's not gonna be able to hear him or talk to him...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Which is why our first priority is to get her to remember him...

dialogues.speaker: Popcorn
dialogues.text: I have to find Homura! I have to help her!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Wait, don't just run off!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: The Little Hexenzirkel wants to help too!

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Homura, the proposal you submitted still has issues. It needs to be more creative, it needs that spark! Back to the drawing board.

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Your ideas were so good when you first started working here. What happened? You know how crucial this pitch is for us. We value your work, but you need to get your head in the game.

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: But, this is already the 12th draft... *sigh* Never mind. Understood.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, that's Homura? Isn't that the girl we met outside of Aisa Bathhouse a few days ago?

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: That person Popcorn keeps ramming into must be her boss. It doesn't seem like either of them can see him...

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Homura still doesn't remember Popcorn. So she can't see him.

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Guess she doesn't wear her hair in pigtails now that she's all grown up, huh.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Well, long hair is a lot of work.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: And no more flowery dresses either...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Well, my mom says pants are easier to work in. But, I suppose it's just a matter of wearing what's comfortable.

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: There's an exhibition being held in a few days. You need to find some time and show the client around. Take good care of him, alright? Our orders for the next year depend on it!

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Oh, and draw up a diagram while you're at it. You're always doodling something or other, aren't you? Doesn't need to look that impressive up close. Just enough to impress the client during the presentation.

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Draw up a sketch. The actual content doesn't matter, just make it look good. We'll change it later depending on the client's feedback.

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Man, that workload is triggering my fight or flight... Or just flight to be honest...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, Homura! Stand up for yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: ...Of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, c'mon! Where's that explosive temper you had as a kid... Like in that poem you wrote!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Wait, that's it! The poem! We can use that to remind her of her childhood, and get her to remember Popcorn!

dialogues.speaker: Prune & Klee
dialogues.text: Bring on the tear-bugs. Bring on the booger-beasts...

dialogues.speaker: Yayao & Qiqi
dialogues.text: Mean, or nasty, or in your face, one punch sends them to outer space!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Give them one great monstrous whack... Wait, what comes next? Sayu?

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Um... Shoot. I think I dozed off during that part...

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Give them one great monstrous whack, then... stuff... stuff 'em in a big ol' sack!

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Yeah, I've got a sack with your name on it!

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Hey! Wait!

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: What is it? Confused about something?

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: I think you're the one who's confused. Your feedback changes from one moment to the next. You don't even know what you want, but somehow, you expect me to read your mind? Maybe if you actually thought things through, we wouldn't have to redo them.

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: You want me to make the decisions? Fine, then don't micromanage me. You nitpick everything I do, just to complain again when I change it. You talk about a lack of creativity, but I don't see you coughing up ideas.

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: You say the company values me? Ha! Really? 'Cause I work myself into the ground every day, and do I even get a free cup of coffee to keep myself awake? No, I buy it myself.

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Of course we plan to reward our hard workers with several level—

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: I'm not done. You wanna talk about rewards? 'Cause it seems like you just reward us with more work. Half the work I do is outside my job description.

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: I'm not a machine. You can't just wind me up and keep me running forever.

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: I'm overworked. I don't get enough sleep, I... I can't keep going on like this.

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: You're my boss. If I can't have your mentorship and guidance, the least you could do is create a suitable working environment.

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Oh, and drawing is what I do for fun, not another thing you get to use to order me around. So just... shut up!

dialogues.speaker: Passing Dog
dialogues.text: Woof! Took the words right out of my mouth!

dialogues.speaker: Passing Cat
dialogues.text: Round of ap-paws! Meow!

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Okay... You're upset. I see that, and... You're right! I put too much on your plate. I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: You should take some time to relax and recharge. How about a three-month paid vacation?

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Ah, of course. Put my Mora where my mouth is, right? I'll add on a three months' bonus. How does that sound?

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: A three months' bonus... three months' bonus... three months' bonus... three months' bonus...

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Ha... Haha... Hahahahahahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Everything... okay?

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Haha... Ha... Hm? Oh, um. Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: You sure?

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Actually, no. Everything is not okay!

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: I think the proposal I submitted is more than competitive enough. Maybe I could talk you through it, and then you can decide whether changes are really necessary.

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: But first... I'd like to take two days off. We can go over it when I get back.

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Is... Is that okay?

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Listen, I get that things come up, but now's not the best time. We're up against some tight deadlines, so just hang in there...

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, but I can't... I have too much work, and it's starting to impact my health. I hope you can understand...

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Huh, you never said anything, and your work is always on time, so I just assumed you could handle it.

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: I complete my work on time because I'm a professional. It's those unreasonable, last-minute tasks that force me to work overtime...

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: And I've been doing that a lot lately... I was hoping you could... be a little more mindful of the work you assign me in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: But, the client is going to be here soon. How am I going to find someone on such short notice?

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Entertaining clients was never part of my job description to begin with...

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Of course, if you really can't approve my time off, I've made peace with having to—

dialogues.speaker: Boss
dialogues.text: Now, hold on just one minute! No need to be rash! How about this? Rest up, get yourself back in working order, and your position will be waiting... Just don't make it too long, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: O—Of course... I'll try.

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Whoa... that was close. I was about to say I'd made peace with having to meet the client...

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Popcorn! It's really you! Oh, and... you're not alone.

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Hello, Miss Homura! We're Popcorn's friends!

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Wait, so... My imaginary friend has real-world friends besides me? This isn't also in my imagination, is it...?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Popcorn explains what happened, with the little witches chiming in with details here and there...

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: I see... Thanks for doing that. I haven't been doing so hot lately, so I've been having nightmares. Sorry you had to go through all that trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Don't worry. The nightmare's been devoured, so you should be able to get a good night's sleep from now on!

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: But the Dough King said you still have mental issues.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Wait, no. That's not... You can't just say that, Qiqi. Adults can't handle being that direct.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, um, anyway... Popcorn said you've been really busy at work?

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Yeah... This is my first job. I was so excited at the start, thinking this was my chance to make a name for myself. But, reality turned out to be pretty harsh...

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Endless work, difficult relationships, and plans that fall through... I couldn't even solve one problem before even bigger ones would pop up.

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: It was suffocating. Even after getting off work, I was too tired to do the things I used to enjoy. All I wanted to do was lie down.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I know exactly what you mean. The adult world is a cold and cruel place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How in the— You're not even an adult!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Huh, I don't get it at all. We all live in the same world, right? Mom said grown-ups are just big kids in grown-up clothes!

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Yeah, I've gathered a lot of intel about this. Turns out, when no one's looking, some grown-ups play their own games too, or put on little puppet shows, or even pretend to cook stuff!

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: I won't say who, though...

dialogues.speaker: Popcorn
dialogues.text: Nothing has to change! We can still fight monsters, or pretend the floor is lava. You just have to picture it, and we can do it!

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Kinda like how I imagined going on that rant just now...? Even though it wasn't real, just picturing it felt pretty cathartic.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: That's not enough, though. Children are innocent. Their fantasies become real to them, so make-believe gives them genuine happiness.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: But adults know it isn't real, so imagination becomes a form of self-deception. It's called a mental escapade.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Oh, right! Yes, that. Shoot... I memorized it wrong.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: The point is, you can't just fantasize about the things that make you happy. You have to take action!

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: That goes for work and regular life. Whether it's "something" or "someone" that's getting you down, you never have to accept the status quo. Just like earlier, saying "no" is the first step.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: And if it continues to stand in your way, just give it the old tear-bug and booger-beast treatment!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! That's the spirit!

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: And if all else goes wrong, I guess the worst-case scenario is... you just find a new job.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that's— Uhh, actually, not sure if that'd be something to celebrate...

response.speaker: Homura
response.text: Huh... I never thought kids would be the ones to give me a much-needed pep talk, but you make some great points. I'll try to take a different approach. Oh, and thanks for everything.

response.speaker: Homura
response.text: You too, Popcorn.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aww. It's so nice seeing Popcorn and Homura together again...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Yeah...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Makes me think about Descartes... Wait a second, what am I even doing!? I've barely made any progress!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Prune? What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I... um... well...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's okay. If you don't want to talk about it, we can pretend we didn't hear anything.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But if you do choose to trust us with it, I'm sure we'd all be more than willing to help out. Right, little witches?

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Yeah! In my heart, Prune is already one of us! We all like you a lot!

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Definitely! We worked super well tracking down those fragments. It's like we were made for each other!

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Plus, our heights all match too! You even taught me how to use a hammer like a pair of stilts, so I could feel what it'd be like to be taller.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Prune knows a lot and likes sharing. She gave me a book on finches.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon seconds all that! Besides, she's so used to you being a part of the Little Hexenzirkel now, she can barely imagine divvying up snacks without counting your share!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: You guys... *sob*... I'm not... I'm not that great...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I've been lying from the start. I'm not Alice's friend!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I'm a Witch Hunter. Witches are my enemies! I'd never be friends with someone like her!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: She challenged me to a debate, and when she lost, she took my imaginary friend away... Like it was nothing! *sobbing*... Descartes is my best friend...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: She said the only way to save him was to defeat all the witches...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I went to Mondstadt to find them, only for the trail to lead me to Inazuma. So I took a boat overnight to get here... and then...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I met you guys instead... It wasn't supposed to be like this!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: You're not evil witches at all, just a group of innocent kids... And... And you've been so nice to me. I can't treat you like my enemies, I just... I can't... *sobbing*

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: It's okay, it's okay. Just let it out.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The little witches stay by Prune's side, holding her hand and patting her on the back, until eventually, she calms down...

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I, um... feel a lot better now. Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: But, uh.... crying like that in front of everyone was super embarrassing. Maybe it could be our little secret?

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: You got it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Prune, could Paimon ask... Did you actually see Alice take Descartes away?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Well, no. I didn't see how she did it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then... did she say how you're supposed to defeat the other witches?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: There were no specifics... But, I'm sure she expects me to fight them or something. That's what a villain would do, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, in our experience, Alice's trials are usually a bit more... unconventional. Besides... she wouldn't be that mean.

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: I don't care what kind of trick she has in store. I'm a Witch Hunter, and that won't change. So, I don't think me and the other little witches can be—

choices.text: You might be at odds with the big witches.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: What?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! The Little Hexenzirkel didn't exist when Alice issued that challenge. You can join, for sure!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Little Hexenzirkel can band together to defeat the big witches and save your imaginary friend!

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: But... Klee is Alice's daughter...

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Um, I'm kinda confused about the details, but I bet it's supposed to be a big, fun game!

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Cause Mom always says I'm gonna beat her one day and become the bestest witch in the whole wide world!

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Catching the big witches sounds like a fun game to me! I wanna play for sure!

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: Sounds like a chance to get in some good training. Count me in.

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: I'm trying to become an even stronger ninja than my sensei too. That way, I can sleep as much as I want and nobody can say a thing.

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: Master said that's called when "the branch grows higher than the tree." We all want that, right, Qiqi?

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: Mm, Qiqi likes trees.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Plus, Paimon and {NICKNAME} have been around the block with all this witch stuff. With us around, we can defeat whatever great, big, powerful, impressive mages we want!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Guess I've been voluntold...

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: You guys... are a really awesome group of kids, you know that?

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Hehe, just give me your hand, and you'll be an official member of the Little Hexenzirkel!

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: I guess I can do kid things with all of you... Ahem, to go along with the group, I mean. Alright, I'll join.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, do the thing!

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: No, I'm not that much of a kid.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Fine, fine. You don't have to give me that look... I'll say it.

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Little witch Prune reporting for duty...

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Ugh, so embarrassing...

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: W—Wait... Is this for real?

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: But, I haven't defeated the witches... Did you escape on your own? Are you hurt? Here, let me see.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what's going on? Is it Descartes?

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Yeah, he's back! He's really back!

response.speaker: Yaoyao
response.text: What did he say?

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: He said... it's a long story, and he'll explain later.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Whoa! A weird-looking dog!

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: What do you mean "weird"? He's adorable! Hold on... You can see him?

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Wait, are these... your imaginary friends? How come I can see them?

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: Wow... look at all of them!

response.speaker: Qiqi
response.text: Tuantuan flew away... She wants to go play over there.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: C'mon, c'mon! Let's go! All the imaginary friends can play together!

response.speaker: Prune
response.text: Wait, what? Wait for me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did you see that? Everyone's imaginary friends are here... in the real world!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's catch up and see what's happening!

choices.text: But that has nothing to do with the Little Hexenzirkel.

talks.objective: Check on the little witches and their imaginary friends

dialogues.text: Real or imaginary... seeing all these friends together like this is a wonderful sight.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: #Hehe... Astute as ever, {NICKNAME}. Consider it a well-earned gift for the Little Hexenzirkel for completing their grand quest!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: I just thought I'd give all our lovely imaginary friends a chance to come out and say hello. What a lively gathering this turned out to be!

choices.text: That's not the only gift, though, is it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! After fixing the whole nightmare situation, Popcorn should've gone back to being a normal imaginary friend. We shouldn't be able to see him, unless...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: You think I would deny my little witches the chance to witness their touching reunion?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Klee would've been devastated if she'd missed it, and I certainly can't have that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, uh... You didn't take Prune's imaginary friend, did you? You don't go around... bullying little kids?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: No, I did not take her imaginary friend.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knew she was right to defend you earlier.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: In fact, when I met little Prune, her imaginary friend was on the verge of disappearing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: You've spent quite a bit of time with her now. What's your impression?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, even though she looks like a small, cute kid, she seems more like a grown-up. She's smart, mature, and super reliable!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Still, it seems like she bottles a lot of things up.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Precisely. Prune has always been a precocious child, ever so curious about the world. She studied things beyond her years and began to grow up rather quickly. I'm sure that all sounds well and good...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: But it's unfair to expect a child to step into the adult world so soon. With all that weight placed on such small shoulders, something is bound to break.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: In this case, her childlike innocence. You've witnessed how devastating the effects of that can be for yourselves, not too long ago.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right, like what happened to Homura... She'll stop dreaming, and eventually, she won't even be able to remember her imaginary friend...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Hah! That's why I made up the whole thing about capturing Descartes and sent her to Mondstadt to "defeat all the witches."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You tricked her! The mages don't even live in Mondstadt! Ugh, that's a mean thing to do to a kid, Alice! Paimon shouldn't have spoken up for you earlier...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Why, thank you for the compliment, dear Paimon. I am the great, big, mean Dodo-King, after all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That means you chose Mondstadt for a different reason...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Ah, well, the seeds of spirit and imagination are best nurtured by the soil of freedom, of course.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It was to give Klee someone else to play with, wasn't it...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Hehe, sharp as a tack, Paimon. The witches of the Little Hexenzirkel do not disappoint.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: In any case, all's well that ends well, right?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: After spending time with the little witches, she regained her childlike innocence and was able to reunite with her imaginary friend.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Ah... Quite the amazing feat the little witches pulled off, huh! The most amazing one of all is my cute little Klee, of course.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Founding the Little Hexenzirkel at such a young age, making her own decisions, accomplishing things all by herself... Don't be shy on the compliments now, okay?

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Honorary Knight! Paimon! Come here, quick!

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Yuegui's teaching Descartes how to do somersaults!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: No matter how precious the moment, it can never last forever. You should head over before the materialization spell wears off, or you might miss the chance to meet everyone's imaginary friends.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Why didn't you say so sooner? Come on, let's go play!

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: It's through embracing our inner child that all of us can wield the magic known as happiness.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: And find our childlike spark and wonder once more.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: So, whether you're a little kid or a kid at heart, set your worries aside for a moment, forget about what's coming next, and allow yourself to have fun — if only just for the here and now.

choices.text: Popcorn's back to normal, but we can still see him...
Your magic did this, didn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: So... it was all a misunderstanding?

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Hmph! That makes it even worse! She tricked me!

dialogues.speaker: Prune
dialogues.text: Hold on, I never said I regretted coming here. And no, I don't regret joining the Little Hexenzirkel either.

dialogues.speaker: Yaoyao
dialogues.text: Whoa, I never thought Gena would be so big!

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Her belly is super soft too. It's a great spot for a nap.

dialogues.speaker: Qiqi
dialogues.text: Hm, very tall. Taller than Sayu.

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Wow, Qiqi... That was cold...

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Oooh, I can warm us all up! Sparks 'n' Splash!

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Are you... disappointed in me, Popcorn? All those dreams I had as a kid, and I haven't achieved a single one. I grew up to be a pathetic adult, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Popcorn
dialogues.text: Can you eat as much tempura as you want, day in and day out?

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Well, I guess...

dialogues.speaker: Popcorn
dialogues.text: Can you buy your favorite light novels and manga without having to ask an adult?

dialogues.speaker: Homura
dialogues.text: Yeah, I make my own Mora, so I can buy whatever I want.

dialogues.speaker: Popcorn
dialogues.text: Then you're an amazing little adult in my book!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, Popcorn's over there! C'mon, let's get closer.
